donnees.titre: Preoperative Topical Steroid Use and Trabeculectomy Outcomes.
donnees.resume:
PRCIS: Preoperative topical steroid use was associated with greater surgical success and thicker, less reflective bleb walls on anterior segment optical coherence tomography 1 year after trabeculectomy.
PURPOSE: To assess the associations of preoperative topical steroid administration with surgical outcomes and filtering bleb morphology 1 year after trabeculectomy.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: This study included 304 eyes from 272 patients who underwent primary trabeculectomy with mitomycin C. Eyes were classified into steroid and nonsteroid groups based on preoperative topical steroid administration for 7 days. The primary outcome was surgical success at 1 year, defined by either criterion A [intraocular pressure (IOP) ≤15 mm Hg and a ≥20% reduction from preoperative IOP] or criterion B (IOP ≤12 mm Hg and a ≥30% reduction from preoperative IOP), achieved without glaucoma medication or additional glaucoma surgery. Bleb morphology was evaluated using anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT). Multivariable Cox regression was used to adjust for potential confounders.
RESULTS: At 1 year, surgical success rates were significantly higher in the steroid group than in the nonsteroid group for both criterion A (85.5% vs. 71.1%, P =0.005) and criterion B (76.4% vs. 65.4%, P =0.040). Preoperative steroid use was significantly associated with a lower hazard of surgical failure (criterion A: adjusted hazard ratio, 0.47; 95% CI: 0.27-0.82; P =0.008). Compared with the nonsteroid group, the steroid group exhibited greater bleb wall thickness (0.812 vs. 0.723 mm, P =0.038) and lower bleb wall reflectivity (130.3 vs. 141.9 arbitrary units, P =0.011).
CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative administration of topical steroids, compared with no steroids, was associated with higher surgical success rates, thicker bleb walls, and lower bleb wall reflectivity on AS-OCT at 1 year.
